summary.title: Operating System in 1,000 Lines
summary.one_liner: Learn to build a small operating system from scratch in C in about 1,000 lines of code, covering context switching, paging, user mode, a shell, a disk driver, and file I/O.
takeaways: Build a small OS kernel step by step in C within roughly 1,000 lines of code.
Implement core OS features: context switching, paging, user mode, a command-line shell, a disk device driver, and file read/write.
Learn OS-specific debugging techniques, since printf debugging is unavailable until output is implemented.
Prerequisites are familiarity with C and a UNIX-like environment; source code is available on GitHub under MIT license.
summary.summary: This online book walks readers through building a minimal operating system from scratch, step by step, in C. It argues that basic kernel functions are simple, noting Linux 0.01 was 8,413 lines, and covers context switching, paging, user mode, a shell, a disk driver, and file operations in about 1,000 lines total. The text warns that debugging is the hardest part and includes guidance on debugging an OS. Code examples are on GitHub, and the book is CC BY 4.0 with MIT-licensed code; it was originally an appendix to the author's Japanese microkernel book.
